newsitem.title: USA: Ex-CIA spy sentenced to over 23 years in jail.
newsitem.headline: Ex-CIA spy sentenced to over 23 years in jail.

text.p: Confessed CIA double-agent Harold Nicholson was sentenced on Thursday to 23 years and seven months in prison for spying for Russia.

Nicholson, 46, pleaded guilty on March 3 to selling national security secrets to Moscow for 2-1/2 years. He was the highest-ranking officer of the Central Intelligence Agency ever convicted of spying.

Nicholson told the court he deeply regretted having sold out his country. "I am in so many ways so very sorry," he said, and added: "I won't ask for forgiveness of my colleagues and countrymen for I know they can't give it."
Nicholson, a divorced father of three, said he had turned to selling secrets to the Russians to get money to compensate his children after "failing to keep my marriage together."

In imposing the sentence, U.S. District Court Judge James Cacheris matched the request of federal prosecutors who struck an agreement with Nicholson under which he admitted guilt and agreed to cooperate in exchange for less than a life sentence.

Nicholson, a former CIA station chief in Romania, confessed to having started spying in June 1994. He acknowledged that he met his Russian handlers four times -- in India, Indonesia, Switzerland and Singapore -- to sell secrets, including the identity of CIA officers.
